_reviewProvenance: Full tier, both directions, run as four host-run Opus agents over the pinned manifest inputs: Direction A across all 24 briefDocs split in two halves, Direction B across all 5 surfaces exhaustively. The pinned context and both direction instructions were passed verbatim so promptHash and manifestHash mean what they claim. 258 elements enumerated; 36 discrepancies. MANIFEST CAVEAT, AND IT IS MATERIAL. manifestHash attests sha256:0afee232... but all three iss35 agents independently found that manifest's pinned context is stale: it names 10 of the 22 files under commands/, omitting reading among others. More seriously, it scopes the search to 04-surfaces/*.md plus 05-internals/08-skills.md, while 6 of Direction B's 13 findings live outside those chapters (01-agents.md, 03-configuration.md, 05-prompt-quality.md, 01-build-sequence.md) -- including all four undocumented cold-reading agents. A run obeying the pinned scope literally would have missed them. The agents were instructed to treat the built binary as ground truth, which the pinned context's own first line directs, and to report manifest staleness separately. So this receipt attests a genuinely full-depth run against an anchor now known to under-cover the record. Re-anchoring the manifest is unfinished work, not a property of this run. DISPOSITIONS. 15 findings are release-introduced (v0.7.0 ships the reading verb and four cold-reading agents that the brief does not document) and 21 are pre-existing prose drift. Both are deferred rather than fixed, and the split is recorded because they are different decisions: the first is this release outrunning its own record, the second is accumulated debt that predates it. The machine-checked layer is clean in both cases -- surface.json against the live binary is byte-exact across 82 command nodes and 109 flags, and every ## Sub-verbs table verified correct. Every finding here is in prose the surface_coverage rule does not scan, which is the gap 04-surfaces/README.md:33 says review must cover. REVIEWED TREE VERSUS SHIPPED TREE. Both passes ran against b5df66c287497064a620bb4e58a546b846733009. This receipt names 4b4076a10f89d4d02da359274dad8994e30cae0e. The delta is four files and every one is a fix responding to these passes: the composer prompt_version bump 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0 with its agents/CHANGELOG.md entry (dc-2, a CI blocker), two recomposed CHANGELOG lines (dc-1 record family, dc-3 five-state), and a fenced-code fix to iss-2609011217083577 that site-render refused. No unreviewed change rides along; `git diff b5df66c2 4b4076a1` is the check. No confirming pass was run against the final commit: that is the maintainer's recorded decision under verifier-selects-gates-decide, disclosed here rather than implied. JUDGE MODEL. claude-opus-5 is the model that ran, recorded as the id available to the harness. It is not a dated snapshot, and the gate does not enforce one: checkReceiptGate requires judgeModel to be non-empty only, so the pinned-snapshot rule the runbook states has no code behind it. Recorded so the receipt does not imply an auditability the gate does not provide.
